en.headline: The Mills hosts free exhibition of rare creatures for Halloween
en.dek: Visitors can see the African pygmy mouse, glowing emperor scorpion and other unusual animals at the Tsuen Wan venue until 1 November.
body: The Mills in Tsuen Wan is hosting a free public exhibition of rare and unusual creatures as part of its Halloween programme, running until 1 November.

Organised with the Hong Kong Insect Education Centre, the Curious Creatures Showcase at Mill 6 ground floor is open daily from noon to 7pm. Displays include the African pygmy mouse, which weighs about five grams, the emperor scorpion that glows under ultraviolet light, the goliath birdeater, and other arthropods, reptiles and small mammals, some making their first public appearance in Hong Kong.

Weekend and public-holiday guided tours lasting about 20 minutes are available on a first-come, first-served basis. The venue said the exhibition is designed to introduce visitors to lesser-known species in a family-friendly setting.

zh.headline: 南豐紗廠萬聖節怪奇動物展覽免費開放至11月1日
zh.dek: 荃灣南豐紗廠與香港昆蟲教育及科普中心合作，展出非洲侏儒鼠、紫外光下會發光的帝王蠍等罕見生物，每日中午至晚上7時開放。
body: 荃灣南豐紗廠今年萬聖節推出「奇蟲物語」活動，當中的萬聖節怪奇動物展覽免費開放至11月1日。
展覽與香港昆蟲教育及科普中心合作，在六廠地下舉行，每日中午12時至晚上7時開放。展品包括體重僅約5克的非洲侏儒鼠、在紫外光下會發出螢光的帝王蠍、世界最大蜘蛛之一的哥利亞食鳥蛛，以及其他節肢動物、爬蟲及小型哺乳類，當中部分物種是香港首次公開展出。
週末及公眾假期設有約20分鐘的導賞團，先到先得。紗廠表示，展覽旨在以適合家庭的方式介紹這些較少見的生物。
